newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks turn south after firm open.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks turn south after firm open.

text.p: Greek equities pulled back from early gains on Monday when blue chips which propped the index higher in the previous week succumbed to selling pressure.

"Today's session provided evidence of the need for higher trading volume to help the index push past the upper limits of its trading range," said Nick Soulimiotis, analyst at Pentedekas Securities. "Unless turnover picks up, the index will remain directionless between 1,570 and 1,640 points."

For the time being, trading interest focuses on stocks affected by current or forthcoming corporate actions such as capital increases -- National Bank, Intracom --, mergers -- insurance and mortgage banks -- and splits -- Goody's, Chipita, said Soulimiotis.

The Athens benchmark index settled 0.48 percent or 7.82 points lower at 1,631.62 from Friday's 1,639.44, coming off a 1,625.11 intraday low recorded around 15 minutes before close. The index peaked at 1,648.76 before mid-session.
Banks and industrials were off 0.52 and 0.36 percent, while construction suffered more, shedding 2.63 percent.
Turnover amounted to 13.2 billion drachmas on volume of 3.3 million shares.
Decliners led advancers 133 to 68 with 28 shares unchanged on 229 traded.
OTE telecom Global Depository Shares (GDS) were quoted on London's SEAQ International market at $11.0-$11.2. Two GDSs make up one share of OTE.
